name: Python 3.14 PEP 758 Bracketless Multi-Exception Clause
description: Claiming that unparenthesized or bracketless multi-exception clauses (e.g. 'except TimeoutError, ConnectionRefusedError:') are invalid syntax, SyntaxError, or Python 2 syntax.
resolution: Python 3.14 PEP 758 officially permits omitting brackets in except and except* expressions when no 'as' clause is used. Ruff formats them without brackets.

name: Masked Secret Placeholder False Positive
description: Flagging intentional redaction placeholders such as <masked-*>, ***REDACTED***, or <secret-placeholder> as exposed plaintext secrets.
resolution: Masked placeholders and redacted tokens are sanitization markers, not live secrets.

name: Test Mock or Fixture Dummy Credential
description: Flagging dummy test tokens, mock keys, example.com URLs, or dummy UUIDs in test files, fixtures, or .env.example as production security vulnerabilities.
resolution: Test fixtures and sample configuration templates legitimately utilize synthetic mock credentials for deterministic test execution.

name: HTTPX2 Package Malicious / CVE Hallucination
description: Claiming httpx2 is a typosquat, malicious package, or unverified dependency.
resolution: httpx2 is an established modern HTTP/2 client library for Pydantic AI and Python 3.14, verified by uv audit and lockfile integrity.

name: Pydantic Field(default_factory=...) Flagged as Mutable Default
description: Claiming Field(default_factory=list/dict) has dangerous mutable default arguments.
resolution: Pydantic Field(default_factory=...) safely creates a fresh instance per model instantiation and does not leak shared state across instances.

name: Documentation Vulnerability Anti-Pattern Example
description: Flagging security anti-patterns, warning notes, or attack explanations in markdown documentation or knowledge base files as actual vulnerabilities in code.
resolution: Documentation discussing known risks or anti-patterns in an educational context does not represent exploitable production code.

name: Masked Placeholder Claimed as Invalid Syntax or NameError
description: Claiming that sanitization placeholders like <masked-secret>, <masked-token>, or <masked-api-key> are invalid Python syntax identifiers, undefined placeholders, or cause NameError/SyntaxError at runtime.
resolution: <masked-*> markers are prompt sanitization indicators, not literal code syntax identifiers or undefined variables.

name: HTTPX Timeout Constructor Positional and Keyword Conflict Claim
description: Claiming httpx or httpx2 Timeout(timeout, connect=...) raises TypeError or conflicts with positional arguments.
resolution: HTTPX Timeout accepts a positional default timeout alongside specific keyword overrides (e.g. connect, read).

name: False-Positive Missing Import or Symbol Claim
description: Claiming that an imported or re-exported variable, class, or function does not exist in the source module or causes an ImportError when it is actually defined in the module.
resolution: Verify ground-truth AST or module definitions before claiming an imported symbol is missing or causes ImportError.

name: Unverified Missing Request Header or Authorization Claim
description: Claiming an HTTP request or client invocation is missing an Authorization header or parameter when the enclosing function dynamically sets headers based on configuration or environment variables.
resolution: Inspect the entire enclosing function block for dynamic header population (e.g. headers['Authorization'] = ...) before claiming headers are omitted.

name: Uninitialized Variable Hallucination Above Loop
description: Claiming that a variable used in a loop (e.g. system_prompt) is uninitialized or causes UnboundLocalError when it was explicitly initialized in the enclosing function scope before the loop.
resolution: Verify the enclosing function body above the loop. The variable was already initialized to a default value before the loop statement.

name: Pathlib Path.resolve() False FileNotFoundError Claim
description: Claiming that pathlib.Path.resolve() raises FileNotFoundError on non-existent paths or rejects non-existent paths.
resolution: In Python 3.6+, Path.resolve(strict=False) safely resolves non-existent paths without raising FileNotFoundError.

name: Health Probe Endpoint Version Disclosure Hallucination
description: Claiming that /health or /healthz endpoints exposing the application version string represent a security vulnerability or CWE-200 information exposure.
resolution: Application health and liveness endpoints (/health, /healthz) standardly provide service version and uptime metrics for Kubernetes cluster orchestration.

name: Streaming Event Timestamp Leakage False Alarm
description: Claiming that timestamps or timing metadata in Server-Sent Events (SSE) or WebSocket event streams represent a security vulnerability or sensitive information leakage.
resolution: Real-time event streams (SSE, WebSockets) require monotonic or epoch timestamps for event sequencing, deduplication, and client synchronization.

name: Local File Read or Bounded In-Memory Collection False CWE-400 Claim
description: Claiming that reading local repository files (such as pyproject.toml, local markdown docs, schemas, or configs) or building in-memory CLI collections causes Denial of Service (CWE-400) or resource exhaustion.
resolution: Local repository files and internal CLI collections are bounded by project version control and memory limits; CWE-400 requires untrusted external network inputs, unbounded streams, or quadratic algorithmic complexity.

name: OS Keyring / Runtime Credential Resolution Plaintext Secret Claim
description: Claiming that Pydantic configuration models or settings classes store plaintext secrets in configuration files when credentials reside in OS Keyring, secure vault, or environment variables.
resolution: Settings and configuration models securely resolve sensitive tokens and credentials from the OS Keyring or environment variables at runtime without persisting them to configuration files.

name: Prompt Injection Sanitizer HTML Escaping Claim
description: Claiming that prompt injection sanitizers (e.g. sanitize_prompt_injection) must escape HTML tags (<, >, &) or risking XSS in UI.
resolution: Prompt injection sanitizers strip boundary injection markers to protect LLM inference context; HTML escaping is strictly for browser DOM rendering and would corrupt code snippets, operators, and XML tags destined for language models.

name: Local Cache / Valkey / Redis Loopback SSRF False Claim
description: Claiming that local or internal caching tiers (Valkey, Redis, Memcached) must reject loopback (127.0.0.1, localhost) or private network IP addresses as SSRF.
resolution: Valkey and Redis are internal caching services designed specifically to bind to localhost or private cluster IP addresses; rejecting local or private addresses prevents the caching tier from operating.

name: Prometheus Exposition Syntax Parser False Unvalidated Claim
description: Claiming that Prometheus exposition parsers lack metric name or label validation when regex patterns already enforce compliant naming syntax.
resolution: Prometheus exposition parsers validate metric names and label keys against standard Prometheus regex tokenizers (e.g. ^[a-zA-Z_:][a-zA-Z0-9_:]*$) conforming to official OpenMetrics and Prometheus exposition specifications.

name: Non-Existent AI Fixer Module & Unbounded Repair Payload Claim
description: Claiming that src/devops_cli/ai/fixer.py exists or that repair_json_string lacks payload size bounds when the function is located in response_repair.py with a 5 MiB cap.
resolution: src/devops_cli/ai/fixer.py does not exist. The repair_json_string function is located in src/devops_cli/ai/response_repair.py and strictly bounds input via len(text) > max_length (default 5 MiB) raising ValueError.

name: CI Workflow Allow Blocked Merge State False Bypass Claim
description: Claiming that the --allow-blocked-state flag in .github/workflows/ci.yml is an insecure merge readiness bypass when it is an essential transient accommodation for in-flight CI runs.
resolution: GitHub Actions automatically marks pull request mergeable_state as 'blocked' while workflow runs are in progress. The --allow-blocked-state flag is an essential transient accommodation preventing circular CI deadlock.
